tables.title: Table 41: Percentage of agricultural households by specific mechanisms to mitigate environmental risks related to inorganic fertilizers use

cells: Table 41:  Percentage of agricultural households by specific mechanisms to mitigate environmental risks related to inorganic fertilizers use
Mechanisms to mitigate environmental risks related to inorganic fertilizers use
Follow protocols as per extension service or retail outlet directions or local regulations, not exceeding recommended doses
Use organic source of nutrients (including manure or composting residues) alone, or in combination with inorganic fertilizers
Use legumes as a cover crop, or component of a multi/crop or pasture system to reduce fertilizer inputs
Distribute synthetic or mineral fertilizer application over the growing period
Consider soil type and climate in deciding fertilizer application doses and frequencies
Use soil sampling at least every 5 years to perform nutrient budget calculations
Perform site-specific nutrient management or precision farming
Use buffer strips along water courses

Adherence to label directions for pesticide use (including use of protection equipment)

tables.title: Table 43: Percentage of Agricultural households by specific mechanisms adopted to avoid environment-related risks associated with use of pesticides

cells: Table 43:  Percentage of Agricultural households by specific mechanisms adopted to avoid environment-related risks associated with use of pesticides
Mechanisms adopted to avoid environment-related risks associated with use of pesticides
Adherence to label directions for pesticide application
Adopt any of the Good Agricultural Practices (GAPs): adjust planting time, apply crop spacing, crop rotation, mixed cropping or inter-cropping Application of crop spacing
Perform biological pest control or use bio pesticides
Adopting pasture rotation to suppress livestock pest population
Systematic removal of plant parts attacked by pest
Maintenance and cleansing of spray equipment after us
Use one pesticide no more than two times or in mixture in a season to avoid pesticide resistance
